summary: Red team of the Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne extraction, against arXiv v2 and the published Acta text: seventeen findings, none high, ten medium, seven low. The extraction is dense and faithful at the level of individual statements, and all sixteen recorded source issues hold. The problems are in ownership and status. (i) Integral excursion algebra: Proposition 8.10 / Corollary 8.11 (item 34) duplicate V. Lafforgue's Proposition 13.1 / Theorem 13.2, already routed to GS.5 by PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18. (ii) Ĝ-pseudocharacter reconstruction: it now has three homes (IHG.1 from this paper; LP2 and GS.5 from Lafforgue's). (iii) Ĝ-valued deformation functors: item 12 duplicates the G-valued lifting Part II of GlobalGaloisDeformations proposed by PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. (iv) Planned items hiding unplanned statements: item 21 is marked planned at SR.1/2/4, although no stage plans the Iwahori–Hecke algebra, the Bernstein presentation or Casselman's theorem; items 32 and 33 contain Chevalley restriction over Z and Definition 8.7 / Lemma 8.8, which are unplanned and unrouted. (v) Key inputs with no item or import: L. Lafforgue's purity (GS.6), Weil II (DWP), function-field Poitou–Tate (ArithmeticGaloisDuality), de Jong/Gaitsgory, Chin, Larsen–Snowden–Wiles and the Levi Galois representations of Proposition 8.12. (vi) The brief: it misstates the theorem's scope and sets impossible tests. (vii) The Theorem 4.10 hypothesis: item 11 and the summary wrongly say it is Schur's lemma for GL_n (a Q_8 counterexample shows otherwise). (viii) Missed paper mistakes: Theorem 11.9 omits the matching of π with φ; Appendix A's strong-regularity reduction is false in general (a G_2 counterexample, though the paper's application is safe); Theorem 5.13's proof needs l > 2; Proposition 5.19 needs S = ∅; and nine smaller slips. (ix) Library: item 3's root data are in Mathlib. (x) Provenance: the review misnames the extraction's author.

It also wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-80, which routes to DeligneWeightsAndPurity and LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles (Weil II 3.2.3/3.3.1 planned at DWP.6/DWP.7); finding 6 cites those stages as the owners of the Weil II input.

Sources, fetched 30 September 2026. arXiv:1609.03491v2 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.03491v2; submitted 29 August 2019; 77 pp.), SHA-256 ec54cf92ce04146c73b48945be2765f675359255d46cc94a0aa35a39229743b9, matching the extraction. The published Acta Math. 223 (2019) 1–111 (https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/acta/2019/0223/0001/ACTA-2019-0223-0001-a001.pdf, 111 pp., printed page = PDF page), SHA-256 15c4b9668e335f75225215bb367c1051769990595232f8015f441d2e2c86ba2c, matching the review. arXiv lists only v1 (12 Sep 2016) and v2; Crossref records no correction or update relation for doi:10.4310/acta.2019.v223.n1.a1. The statement numbering of v2 and the published text agrees (all numbered statements compared). Every paper mistake filed here was located in both texts.

The whole paper re-read against the v2 text layer, in four parallel section passes (§§1–4; §§5–7; §8; §§9–11 and Appendices A–B). Page images were rendered at 150–300 dpi where hats, bars and indices matter (pp. 6, 7, 10, 15–18, 20, 21, 23, 26, 30, 31, 37–41, 43–50, 54, 63, 65, 68, 71). Every finding filed was re-checked personally at its page. All 36 items against the paper. Statements and hypotheses are faithful apart from findings 1, 5, 12, 14, 15 and 16. Route 4 (Theorem 4.8 → R01.1) and route 5 (§9 → R23.1) are sound apart from the .md wording of route 5 (finding 17).

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19.result.json: item /11 (statement and note), summary; route 3 reason (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants); route 1 brief ('Keep the hypotheses visible'); research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19.md §'What the paper proves'
findings.claim: Item 11 says of Theorem 4.10's hypothesis (the centralizer of ρ̄ in Ĝ^ad_k is scheme-theoretically trivial): 'for Ĝ = GL_n the hypothesis is equivalent to irreducibility by Schur's lemma, but in general it is strictly stronger'. The note calls it the general-group analogue 'with "scheme-theoretically trivial centralizer in Ĝ^ad" in place of absolute irreducibility'. The summary says 'For GL_n that hypothesis is Schur's lemma and the statement is Carayol's', and the brief says 'the scheme-theoretically trivial centralizer in Ĝ^ad, which for GL_n is Schur's lemma'. This is false: for Ĝ = GL_n the Ĝ^ad-hypothesis is strictly stronger than absolute irreducibility. Counterexample: l odd, Q_8 ⊂ SL_2(F̄_l) ⊂ GL_2(F̄_l) with its 2-dimensional representation. It is absolutely irreducible, and its centralizer in GL_2 is the scalars. But its image in PGL_2 is the Klein group V_4, which is abelian, so V_4 lies in its own centralizer in PGL_2 = Ĝ^ad: the centralizer is non-trivial and Theorem 4.10 does not apply, although Carayol's theorem does. The paper's Schur sentence (§1(i)) is about a different condition, the centralizer in Ĝ being the centre of Ĝ; the extraction transferred it to the Ĝ^ad hypothesis. A builder following the brief would state Theorem 4.10 as a generalization of Carayol that specializes to it, which it does not.
findings.evidence: Theorem 4.10, v2 p. 17 (published p. 25): 'suppose further that the centralizer of ρ̄ in Ĝ^ad_k is scheme-theoretically trivial'. §1(i), v2 p. 3 (published p. 3): 'The key hypothesis we impose is that the centralizer in Ĝ of the representation being deformed is as small as possible, i.e. the centre of Ĝ. If Ĝ = GL_n, then Schur's lemma says that this condition is equivalent to irreducibility'. Carayol [Car94] and Rouquier need only absolute irreducibility; the Q_8 computation above shows the gap.
findings.fix: In item 11, the summary, the route 3 reason, the brief and the .md, replace the GL_n sentence with: 'For Ĝ = GL_n the hypothesis (trivial centralizer in PGL_n) implies absolute irreducibility but is strictly stronger (e.g. Q_8 ⊂ SL_2, whose image in PGL_2 is centralized by V_4); Theorem 4.10 therefore does not recover Carayol's theorem in full, and IHG.1's Carayol–Rouquier statement remains the GL_n owner.' Add the §1(i) sentence as a new source issue (finding 13).

findings.claim: Item 34 (Proposition 8.10 and Corollary 8.11) is routed to the new Part II as new construction. But Proposition 8.10's content is V. Lafforgue's Proposition 13.1 plus his Lemme 10.5, and the paper says so. That the O-algebra generated inside End_O of a finite free O-module is finite flat is immediate. Corollary 8.11 is Theorem 4.5 applied to the result, and is Lafforgue's Theorem 13.2 at an F̄_l-point. PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 (accepted) already routes Proposition 13.1 and Theorem 13.2 as item PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18/41 in a source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5, so this mathematics has two owners. The note's claim that 'PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18's own §13 gives the F̄_ℓ-coefficient statement but not the finite flat integral algebra B(U, O)' is wrong: /41 states that the O_E-lattice is preserved by every excursion operator. The note's second claim, that Corollary 8.11 is 'the point at which the invariant theory of §3.2 over a DVR is used', is also wrong. The proof of Corollary 8.11 applies Theorem 4.5, over an algebraically closed field; §3.2 enters through Theorem 4.10, in Lemma 8.19.

findings.claim: Several key theorems the paper uses as inputs are neither items nor imports in the brief, so the Part II design job will not wire them. (1) L. Lafforgue [Laf02, Théorème VII.6] (punctual purity of weight 0, and the compatible systems of GL_n-representations), used in Proposition 5.12 and Theorem 6.5. It is planned at GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.6 ('purity … conclusions in the exact theorem range'), but GS.6 is not in the brief's import list. (2) The Weil II bound that H^j(X̄−S̄, F) of a lisse sheaf punctually pure of weight 0 is mixed of weights ≥ j, used in Proposition 5.12. It is planned at DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.6–DWP.7 (with Poincaré duality), not imported. Disclosure: this session wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-80, whose source route feeds DWP.5–DWP.8 and which marks Weil II 3.2.3 planned at DWP.6 and 3.3.1 at DWP.7; this finding cites those stages. (3) The global Euler characteristic formula and Cassels–Poitou–Tate for Γ_{K,S} over a function field ([Mil06, Thm 5.1], [Čes, Thm 6.2]), used in Propositions 5.11, 5.19 and 11.2. The accepted PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22/6 routes exactly these function-field cases to ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3/R02.4, which the brief does not import. (4) De Jong's conjecture ([Gai07, Thm 3.6]), the engine of Theorem 5.13, planned nowhere (PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22/63: 'de Jong's conjecture is not in the atlas'). (5) Chin's independence-of-l theorem [Chi04, Thms 1.4, 4.6, 6.12, Lemma 6.4], (6) Larsen's maximality in the form [SW, Prop. 7.1], and (7) Völklein's H^1(Ĝ(F_l), ĝ) = 0: all used as black boxes in §6 and planned nowhere. (8) The mod-l Galois representations ρ̄_i : Γ_K → M̂(k) attached to cuspidal representations of every proper Levi M, which Proposition 8.12 takes as input data but which the proof of Lemma 8.16 never constructs (V. Lafforgue for the reductive group M, integrally). Only the prerequisites list mentions (1), (4), (5) and (6), which does not make them items (PROTOCOL §16: 'Every definition, construction and key theorem the paper uses … is an item').

findings.claim: The brief is the design job's instructions, and two of its statements are wrong. (a) It opens 'prove the converse direction … potentially and for every reductive group'. The theorem is for G split semisimple, and §§5–11 assume Ĝ semisimple (from §5 on), with simply connected simple Ĝ in §§10–11. (b) Its acceptance tests cannot be met by what the Part II builds. 'GL_n/PGL_n must recover L. Lafforgue's theorem with K′ = K': GL_n is not semisimple, and the paper's method gives only a finite extension K′ (the paper: 'One expects that this theorem should be true with K′ = K, but we are not able to prove this'); for PGL_n the K′ = K statement comes from [Laf02], not from this Part II. 'A torus must recover class field theory': tori are excluded by the standing hypothesis that Ĝ is semisimple. 'The r = 0 count of Taylor–Wiles places must degenerate correctly': r = rank Ĝ = 0 means Ĝ is trivial.
findings.evidence: v2 p. 1 (§1): 'let G be a split semisimple algebraic group over F_q'; v2 p. 18 (§5): 'Ĝ split semisimple' (as quoted in item 12's statement: 'Standing hypotheses from §5 on: Ĝ split semisimple over Z'); v2 p. 2: 'One expects that this theorem should be true with K′ = K, but we are not able to prove this.' Brief: 'Tests: GL_n/PGL_n must recover L. Lafforgue's theorem with K′ = K; a torus must recover class field theory; the r = 0 count of Taylor–Wiles places must degenerate correctly.'
findings.fix: Replace 'for every reductive group' with 'for every split semisimple group G'. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry); item /28 (Appendix A statement: 'One reduces to Ē_Ť strongly regular by embedding G in G ×^{Z(G)} T′')
findings.claim: Missed mistake in Gaitsgory's Appendix A, §3. The reduction to strongly regular Ē_Ť rests on the claim 'E_Ť1 is automatically strongly regular. This follows from the fact that the derived group of G_1 is simply connected', which is false in general. The definition itself is misprinted ('non-isomorphic to Ē_Ť^{w′} for any w′ ∈ W' must exclude w′ = 1). Counterexample: G = G_2, which is simply connected and adjoint, so Z(G) = 1, G_1 = G_2 × T′ and both derived groups are simply connected. Take an elliptic curve X/F_q whose Frobenius acts on X[2] with order 3, and let E_Ť be the Ť[2]-torsor obtained from [2] : X → X by an identification X[2] ≅ Ť[2] carrying Frobenius to the action of a Coxeter element w. The Coxeter element acts on Ť[2] with order 3: w^3 = −1 is trivial there, and w is non-trivial there because Ť^w = Z_Ǧ = 1. Then Fr^*Ē_Ť ≅ Ē_Ť^w. The induced Weil Ǧ-local system is irreducible: its image ⟨Ť[2], w̃⟩ is finite, and a torus centralizing it would lie in the identity component of Z(Ť[2]), which is Ť because no root of G_2 is divisible by 2 in the root lattice, and so in Ť^w, which is finite. But w′ = −1 ∈ W acts trivially on Ť[2], so Ē_Ť^{−1} ≅ Ē_Ť, and likewise for Ē_Ť1: strong regularity fails. The orthogonality [BG08, Prop. 10.6] used for (11.14) needs strong regularity, so the general argument of Appendix A has a gap. The paper's application is unaffected: for a Coxeter parameter the geometric monodromy contains v ∈ T̂[t]^{w=q} with Stab_W(v) = 1 (proof of Proposition 10.2(iv)), so strong regularity holds directly. Item 28 states the reduction as valid.
findings.evidence: v2 p. 68 (published: same, Appendix A §3): '3. First, we claim that we can assume that E_Ť is strongly regular, i.e., E_Ť is non-isomorphic to E_Ť^{w′} for any w′ ∈ W. Indeed, embed G into G_1 := G ×^{Z(G)} T′ … We claim that E_Ť1 is automatically strongly regular. This follows from the fact that the derived group of G_1 is simply connected.' v2 p. 54 (Proposition 10.2 proof): 'suppose that v is not regular semisimple, hence that the stabilizer of v in W is non-trivial (because Ĝ is assumed simply connected)'.
findings.fix: Add a source issue (kind error, affects the proof of Appendix A's general cuspidality claim, known new). Correction: replace the claim by the hypothesis that Ē_Ť is strongly regular (w′ ≠ 1), and note that it holds for the Ť-local systems attached to Coxeter parameters (Stab_W(v) = 1), which is the only case Theorem 10.11 needs. In item 28, state Appendix A under that hypothesis instead of presenting the reduction as valid.

findings.claim: Missed mistake in the introduction. It describes 'the key hypothesis' of Theorem 4.10 as 'the centralizer in Ĝ of the representation being deformed is as small as possible, i.e. the centre of Ĝ' and says that for GL_n this is equivalent to irreducibility. Both halves are inexact. First, Theorem 4.10's hypothesis is triviality of the centralizer in Ĝ^ad, which is stronger even for GL_n (the Q_8 ⊂ SL_2 example of finding 1 has centralizer the centre in GL_2, but a non-trivial centralizer in PGL_2). Second, a scalar commutant in GL_n does not give irreducibility without semisimplicity: a non-split extension of two distinct characters has scalar centralizer. This slip is the source of finding 1.
findings.evidence: v2 p. 3; published p. 3: 'The key hypothesis we impose is that the centralizer in Ĝ of the representation being deformed is as small as possible, i.e. the centre of Ĝ. If Ĝ = GL_n, then Schur's lemma says that this condition is equivalent to irreducibility (i.e. that the image be contained in no proper parabolic subgroup of Ĝ), but in general this condition is strictly stronger.' Theorem 4.10, v2 p. 17: 'the centralizer of ρ̄ in Ĝ^ad_k is scheme-theoretically trivial'.

findings.claim: Missed gap in Proposition 5.19 when S ≠ ∅. The proof writes the Cassels–Poitou–Tate sequence as 0 → H^1_{Q-triv}(Γ_{K,S∪Q}, ĝ^∨_k(1)) → H^2(Γ_{K,S∪Q}, ĝ_k) → ⊕_{v∈Q}H^2(K_v, ĝ_k) → 0, and deduces from Q = ∅ that h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ_k) = h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ^∨_k(1)). By Poitou–Tate, however, the kernel is Ш^1_{S∪Q}(ĝ^∨_k(1)): classes trivial at every place of S ∪ Q, not only at Q. (Using H^2(K_v, ĝ_k) = 0 for v ∈ S, the kernel of the map to ⊕_{v∈Q} equals the kernel of the map to ⊕_{v∈S∪Q}.) So the Q = ∅ case gives h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ_k) = h^2(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ_k) = dim Ш^1_S(ĝ^∨_k(1)) ≤ h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ^∨_k(1)). Equality needs the localization H^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ^∨_k(1)) → ⊕_{v∈S}H^1(K_v, ĝ^∨_k(1)) to vanish, and the hypothesis H^0(K_v, ĝ^∨_k(1)) = 0 does not give that: h^1(K_v, ĝ^∨_k(1)) = h^0(K_v, ĝ_k), which can be non-zero. Assertion (i) and the count in (iii) are therefore not proved for S ≠ ∅. The consequence r#Q = h^1(Γ_{K,S∪Q}, ĝ_k) survives, because Ш ⊂ H^1_{Q-triv} = 0. This is harmless in the paper: the only application is S = ∅ (v2 p. 48, 'Let q = h^1(Γ_{K,∅}, ĝ_k). By Proposition 5.19'). Item 18 states the proposition as printed, and E8's reasoning relies on the same Q = ∅ equality.
findings.evidence: v2 pp. 23–24 (published p. 34): '(i) … #Q = h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ_k) = h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ^∨_k(1)). (ii) We have h^1_{Q-triv}(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ^∨_k(1)) = 0. (By definition, this is the dimension of the kernel of the map H^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ^∨_k(1)) → ⊕_{v∈Q}H^1(K_v, ĝ^∨_k(1)).)'; then the displayed sequence and 'the case Q = ∅ gives the equality h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ_k) = h^1(Γ_{K,S}, ĝ^∨_k(1))'.
findings.fix: Add a source issue (kind gap, affects a stated result for S ≠ ∅, known new). Correction: either restrict Proposition 5.19 to S = ∅, or add the hypothesis H^0(K_v, ĝ_k) = 0 for v ∈ S (so that H^1(K_v, ĝ^∨_k(1)) = 0), or define the Selmer group as Ш^1_{S∪Q}. Record the restriction in item 18, and note it in E8's reason.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry); items /5, /14, /23, /25, /35 and the recorded E12(e)
findings.claim: Further verified slips in the paper that no source issue records. (a) v2 p. 20, proof of Proposition 5.12: 'H is reductive, because ρ_f is absolutely Ĝ-irreducible; and then semisimple, because Ĝ is semisimple'. This is false: N(T) ⊂ SL_2 is Ĝ-irreducible with identity component a torus. The needed conclusion (the constituents of ĝ_E have finite-order determinant) still holds, because the connected centre of H° has no non-trivial H-invariant characters, H being Ĝ-irreducible with finite centralizer. Item 14 repeats the chain. (b) v2 p. 10: 'l is a very good characteristic for G if it is very good for each of the simple factors of G. In this case g is a semisimple Lie algebra'. This is false for reductive non-semisimple G (a torus, GL_n); it is harmless for semisimple Ĝ. Item 5 copies it. (c) v2 p. 52, Theorem 9.3(ii) ([MB90] as quoted): 'For each place w of M above a place v of S … there is an isomorphism M_w ≅ M_v … such that the composite … equals ϕ_v'. Changing w within the fibre over v′ conjugates the composite by ϕ(g); requiring equality at every w forces H = C_H(D)·D for D = ϕ_v(Gal(M_v/K_v)), which fails e.g. for H = S_3 and D of order 2. It should read 'for some place w' (or 'up to H-conjugacy'). Item 23 copies 'at each place above S'. (d) v2 p. 54, proof of Proposition 10.2: 'The characteristic polynomial in F_t[X] of w acting on T̂(k)[t] has distinct roots.' This is false in type D_{2m}: for D_4 the exponents 1, 3, 3, 5 give a repeated eigenvalue. Only the multiplicity one of q (exponent 1) is used. (e) v2 p. 30, proof of Lemma 7.3: 'Let U_p ⊂ U denote the maximal pro-p-subgroup; then … U/U_p ≅ T(F_q)'. U = G(O_K) surjects onto G(F_q) and has no such quotient; it should be U_0/U_p, with U_p the pro-p radical of the Iwahori. (f) v2 p. 13, proof of Proposition 3.13: 'η⫽G : X′⫽G → X⫽G is étale at i(1, x)'. This should be π_{X′}(i(1, x)), and p. 12's 'the action map G × S → X is étale at x' should be at (1, x); E12(e) records only 'G_k·φ(x)'. (g) v2 p. 38, Lemma 8.8: 'for almost every place v of K such that π^{G(O_{K_v})} ≠ 0' (twice) should be π_v. (h) v2 pp. 11–12, proof of Lemma 3.11: the final 'one more application of Lemma 3.12' takes A = O[X]^G with L the Galois closure over Frac O[X]. But Lemma 3.12 needs L/Frac A Galois, and L is not algebraic over Frac O[X]^G when G has positive-dimensional orbits (as in Proposition 3.13, where X′ ⊃ G × S). A gap, repaired by replacing L with the algebraic closure of Frac O[X]^G in L. (i) v2 pp. 40–41, proof of Proposition 8.12: absolute strong irreducibility (Definition 3.5(ii), quantified over ρ′ : Γ → G(k)) is applied to ρ̄_i ⊗ λ valued in Ĝ(l), l ⊋ k; the definition must quantify over G(k̄). All of (a)–(i) are also in the published text.
findings.evidence: Quotations as given in the claim, all checked in the arXiv v2 text layer (with renders of pp. 21, 54 and 65 where hats or bars matter) and located in the published text. Definition 3.5(ii), v2 p. 9: 'for any other homomorphism ρ′ : Γ → G(k) such that … ρ′ is also absolutely G-irreducible'; Proposition 8.12 proof, v2 p. 40: 'the elements ρ̄_{i0}(Frob_v) and (ρ̄_i ⊗ λ)(Frob_v) ∈ Ĝ(l) … Applying the strong irreducibility property of ρ̄_{i0}'.
findings.fix: Add these as source issues: (a), (h) and (i) as gaps affecting the proof; (b)–(g) as misprints affecting nothing (or extend E12(e) with (f)). Adjust items 5 (restrict 'g is semisimple' to semisimple G), 14 (give the correct reason) and 23 ('for some place w above each v ∈ S').
